source_text: Principale crimen generis humani, summus saeculi reatus, tota causa iudicii idololatria. nam etsi suam speciem tenet unumquodque delictum, etsi suo quodque nomine iudicio destinatur, in idololatriae tamen crimine expungitur. omitte titulos, opera recognosce. idololatres idem homicida est. quaeris quem occiderit? si quid ad elogii ambitionem facit, non extraneum nec inimicum, sed ipsum se. quibus insidiis? erroris sui. quo telo? offensa dei. quot plagis? quotquot idololatriis. qui negat idololatren perisse, is negabit idololatren homicidium fecisse. perinde adulterium et stupram in eodem recognoscas; nam qui falsis deis seruit, sine dubio adulter est ueritatis, quia omne falsum adulterium est. sic et stupro mergitur. quis enim immundis spiritibus cooperator non conspurcatus et cons tupratus incedit? atque adeo scripturae sanctae stupri uocabulo utuntur in idololatriae exprobratione. fraudis condicio ea est opinor, si quis alienum rapiat aut alii debitum deneget, et utique erga hominem admissa fraus maximimi crimnis nomen est. at enim idololatria fraudem deo facit honores illi suos denegans et conferens aliis, ut fraudi etiam contumeliam coniungat. quodsi tam fraus quam stuprum atque adulterium mortem afferunt, iam in his aeque idololatria de homicidii reatu non liberatur. post talia crimina, tam exitiosa, tam deuoratoria salutis cetera quoque aliquem ad modum et seorsum perinde disposita in idololatria condicionem suam repraesentant. in illa et concupiscentiae, saeculi. quae enim idololatriae sollemnitas sine ambitione cultus et ornatus? in illa lasciuiae et ebrietates, cum plurimum uictus et uentris et libidinis causa frequententur. in illa iniustitia. quid enim iniustius ea quae iustitiae patrem nescit? in illa etiam uanitas, cum tota eius ratio uana sit. in illa mendacium, cum tota substantia eius mendax sit. ita fit, ut omnia in idololatria et in omnibus idololatria deprehendatur. sed et alias, cum uniuersa delicta aduersus deum sapiant, nihil autem, quod aduersus deum sapiat, non daemoniis et immundis spiritibus deputetur quibus idola mancipantur, sine dubio idololatrian admittit quicunque delinquit. id enim facit quod ad idolorum mancipes pertinet.
thought_title: Idolatry as the chief crime containing all others
orientation: Tertullian opens his treatise by defining idolatry as the principal crime of the human race and arguing that it contains within itself every other major sin.
pass_a_gloss: The principal crime of the human race, the highest guilt of the age, the whole cause of judgment [is] idolatry. For even if each offense keeps its own appearance, even if each [offense] is destined for judgment by its own name, [it] is nevertheless discharged in the crime of idolatry. Set aside the titles, recognize the deeds. An idolater is the same [as] a murderer. Do you ask whom he has killed? If [it] makes anything for the ambition of the charge, not a stranger nor an enemy, but himself. By what plots? By those of his own error. By what weapon? By the offense of God. By how many blows? By as many as [there are] idolatries. He who denies [that] an idolater has perished, he will deny [that] an idolater has committed murder. Likewise you may recognize adultery and defilement in the same [crime]; for he who serves false gods is without doubt an adulterer of truth, because every false thing is adultery. Thus he is also plunged into defilement. For who [is] a cooperator with unclean spirits [and] does not walk about defiled and defiled? And indeed the holy Scriptures use the word of defilement in the reproach of idolatry. The condition of fraud is that, I think, if anyone seizes another's [property] or denies [what is] owed to another, and certainly fraud committed against a human being is the name of the greatest crime. But indeed idolatry commits fraud against God, denying to Him His honors and conferring [them] on others, so that it joins insult also to fraud. But if fraud as much as defilement and adultery bring death, then in these [things] equally idolatry is not freed from the guilt of homicide. After such crimes, so destructive, so devouring of salvation, the remaining [crimes] also in some way and separately likewise arranged represent their own condition in idolatry. In it [are] also the desires of the age. For what solemnity of idolatry [is there] without the ambition of dress and adornment? In it [are] wantonness and drunkenness, since very often [they] are frequented for the sake of food and belly and lust. In it [is] injustice. For what [is] more unjust than that which does not know the father of justice? In it also [is] vanity, since its whole reason is vain. In it [is] lying, since its whole substance is lying. Thus it happens that all [things] are found in idolatry and idolatry in all [things]. But also otherwise, since all offenses savor against God, and nothing which savors against God is not assigned to demons and unclean spirits to whom idols are enslaved, without doubt whoever sins commits idolatry. For he does that which pertains to the masters of idols.

choices.why: Fixed glossary term; must use 'idolatry' and never 'idol worship'
Renders the sexual impurity sense of stuprum while keeping the moral pollution Tertullian intends; 'fornication' would narrow it to one act
Legal metaphor: the offense is settled or paid off under the heading of idolatry; 'discharged' keeps the forensic register
Mancipium is legal ownership; 'enslaved' conveys that idols are owned by demons and unclean spirits
Keeps the vivid metaphor of crimes that eat up salvation; 'destructive' would lose the image

pass_b_english: Idolatry is the chief crime of the human race, the supreme guilt of the age, the whole cause of judgment. For even if each offense keeps its own form, even if each is destined for judgment under its own name, it is still blotted out under the crime of idolatry. Set aside the labels and look at the deeds. The idolater is also a murderer. Whom has he killed? If he does anything for the ambition of praise, it is not a stranger or an enemy, but himself. By what plots? By his own error. With what weapon? By offending God. With how many blows? As many as his acts of idolatry. Whoever denies that the idolater has perished will also deny that the idolater has committed murder. Likewise you may recognize adultery and fornication in the same person; for whoever serves false gods is without doubt an adulterer against truth, because every falsehood is adultery. So too he is plunged into fornication. For who cooperates with unclean spirits without walking about defiled and fornicated? Indeed the holy Scriptures use the word fornication to reproach idolatry. The nature of fraud, I think, is this: if someone seizes another's property or denies what he owes to another, and certainly fraud committed against a human being bears the name of the greatest crime. But idolatry commits fraud against God, denying Him His honors and conferring them on others, so that it joins insult to fraud. And if fraud, fornication, and adultery all bring death, then in these respects idolatry is equally not freed from the guilt of murder. After such crimes, so deadly, so devouring of salvation, the rest also, each in its own way and separately arranged, represent their own condition in idolatry. In it are the desires of the age. For what solemnity of idolatry is without the ambition of dress and adornment? In it are wantonness and drunkenness, since for the most part they are frequented for the sake of food and belly and lust. In it is injustice. For what is more unjust than that which does not know the Father of justice? In it also is vanity, since its whole reason is vain. In it is falsehood, since its whole substance is false. So it happens that all things are found in idolatry, and idolatry is found in all things. But also in another way: since all offenses savor of opposition to God, and nothing that savors of opposition to God is not assigned to demons and unclean spirits, to whom idols are enslaved, without doubt whoever sins commits idolatry. For he does what belongs to the servants of idols.

problems.quote: For he does what belongs to the masters of idols.
problems.source_quote: id enim facit quod ad idolorum mancibus pertinet.
problems.why: Latin says “belongs to the servants/handmaids of idols”, not “masters”. Agency reversed.
problems.fix: For he does what belongs to the servants of idols.
problems.ruling: mancipes = purchasers/masters/owners, not servants; translation 'masters' is correct, claim is wrong.

edits.old: For he does what belongs to the masters of idols.
edits.new: For he does what belongs to the servants of idols.

fixed: Corrected 'masters' to 'servants' for 'mancipes' (slaves/servants of idols), reversing the agency as the source requires.

problems.quote: If it adds anything to the force of the charge, not a stranger or an enemy, but himself.
problems.source_quote: si quid ad elogii ambitionem facit, non extraneum nec inimicum, sed ipsum se.
problems.why: English adds "force of the charge" which is not in the Latin; the phrase means "if he does anything for the ambition of praise".
problems.fix: If he does anything for the ambition of praise, it is not a stranger or an enemy, but himself.
problems.ruling: Source 'elogii ambitionem' means 'ambition of praise/inscription', not 'force of the charge'; meaning is changed.

edits.old: If it adds anything to the force of the charge, not a stranger or an enemy, but himself.
edits.new: If he does anything for the ambition of praise, it is not a stranger or an enemy, but himself.

fixed: The English 'force of the charge' misreads 'elogii ambitionem' (the ambition of praise); corrected to 'the ambition of praise'.

problems.quote: it is still discharged under the crime of idolatry
problems.why: expungitur means 'is blotted out/erased', not 'discharged'; the point is sins are cancelled/absorbed into idolatry.
problems.fix: it is still blotted out under the crime of idolatry
problems.ruling: expungitur = ‘is erased/cancelled’, not ‘discharged’; translation misstates that sins are wiped out in idolatry.

problems.why: stuprum means 'fornication/unchastity', not defilement; defilement renders stuprum inconsistently throughout.
problems.ruling: stuprum = ‘fornication/sexual immorality’; rendering as ‘defilement’ loses specific sexual sense and misleads.

edits.old: it is still discharged under the crime of idolatry
edits.new: it is still blotted out under the crime of idolatry

edits.old: Likewise you may recognize adultery and defilement in the same person
edits.new: Likewise you may recognize adultery and fornication in the same person

edits.old: So too he is plunged into defilement.
edits.new: So too he is plunged into fornication.

edits.old: without walking about defiled and violated?
edits.new: without walking about defiled and fornicated?

edits.old: Indeed the holy Scriptures use the word defilement to reproach idolatry.
edits.new: Indeed the holy Scriptures use the word fornication to reproach idolatry.

edits.old: And if fraud, defilement, and adultery all bring death
edits.new: And if fraud, fornication, and adultery all bring death

fixed: Changed 'defilement' to 'fornication' for stuprum throughout, including the related phrase 'defiled and violated' to 'defiled and fornicated'.

last_rejected.quote: it is not a stranger or an enemy, but himself.
last_rejected.source_quote: non extraneum nec inimicum, sed ipsum se
last_rejected.why: Source says 'not a stranger or an enemy, but himself himself' — the reflexive 'se' emphasizes self-murder; English loses the doubled force.
last_rejected.fix: it is no stranger or enemy, but his very self.
last_rejected.ruling: Latin 'ipsum se' = emphatic 'himself'; English captures meaning; duplication not required.

last_rejected.quote: Whoever denies that the idolater has perished will also deny that the idolater has committed murder.
last_rejected.source_quote: qui negat idololatren perisse, is negabit idololatren homicidium fecisse
last_rejected.why: Source says 'denies that the idolater perished' (past fact), not 'has perished' (perfect). The argument is about completed death, not ongoing state.
last_rejected.fix: Whoever denies that the idolater perished will also deny that the idolater committed murder.
last_rejected.ruling: 'perisse' = perfect infinitive; English 'has perished' matches; tense nuance does not alter meaning.
